title: Sovereign green bonds: a catalyst for sustainable debt market development?
summary: This BIS Working Paper (No. 1198) examines whether sovereign green bond issuance catalyzes private sustainable bond market development. Using empirical analysis, the authors find that sovereign green bond debuts are associated with increased number and size of corporate green bond issuance, improved green verification standards, and narrowed yield spreads for corporate green bonds in the same jurisdiction.
key_points: Sovereign issuers entered sustainable bond markets as 'latecomers' after corporates, contrary to the typical sovereign-first bond market development sequence
Empirical results show both the number and size of corporate green bond issuance increase after sovereign green bond debut in a jurisdiction
The effect is more pronounced in countries with stronger climate policies
Sovereign debut improves quality of green verification standards in corporate bond markets more generally
Sovereign green bond issuance increases liquidity and diminishes yield spreads for corporate green bonds
Historical bond market development literature confirms sovereign securities serve as benchmarks and promote vibrant corporate bond markets
why_it_matters: Understanding whether sovereign green bond issuance catalyzes private market development is relevant for policy makers weighing the costs and benefits of sovereign green issuance programs. For investors, it suggests potential spillover effects from sovereign green issuance to corporate green bond markets, affecting liquidity and spreads.
